Chief_Complaint.content: Patient reports 4 days of feeling 'under the weather' with sore throat, runny nose, dry cough, and fatigue.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: 4 days “under the weather” — sore throat + runny nose → now dry cough; fatigue

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Sore throat for 2 days with initially painful swallowing, now improving.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sore throat x2 days, painful swallow initially; improving

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rhinorrhea and nasal congestion are present.
Fever earlier in the illness, improving with paracetamol and naproxen.
Shortness of breath on exertion, none at rest, and no chest pain.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: SOB on exertion; none at rest; no CP

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Intermittent generalized headaches without visual changes or photophobia.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Headaches intermittent, generalized; no visual changes; no photophobia

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No nausea or vomiting; bowel and urinary habits are normal.
Decreased appetite and increased fluid intake.
Myalgias and joint aches over the past couple of days.
Exposure to coworker with upper respiratory infection and possible daycare exposure via coworker’s children.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Exposure: coworker with URI; possible daycare exposure via coworker’s kids

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Overall 4-day course with sore throat (improving), rhinorrhea/congestion, new dry cough, myalgias, initial fever now settling, night sweats, and mild dyspnea on exertion without red flag symptoms.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: 4-day course with sore throat (improving), rhinorrhea/congestion, new dry cough, myalgias, initial fever now settling; night sweats; mild DOE; no red flags (no CP, no rest SOB, no N/V, no rash)

Medications.content: Plan to continue paracetamol as antipyretic/analgesic.
May use ibuprofen as advised for symptom control.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as an accountant and is still working.
Patient experiences work stress around year-end but reports mood is okay.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: work stress around year-end but mood OK

Assessment.content: Viral upper respiratory tract infection versus early influenza is suspected.
No red flags identified: no chest pain, no shortness of breath at rest, no nausea or vomiting, no rash.
Assessment.source_text: no red flags (no CP, no rest SOB, no N/V, no rash)

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise rest and consider 1–2 days off work.
Encourage oral hydration and increased fluid intake.
Continue paracetamol for antipyretic and analgesic effect.
May use ibuprofen as advised for additional symptom relief.

Follow_up_Information.content: Return for review if not improving by next week.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Return if not improving by next week

Follow_up_Information.content: Seek earlier review or phone consultation if high fever recurs, shortness of breath worsens, or chest pain develops.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Safety-net: earlier review/phone if high fever recurs, worsening SOB, or chest pain

Review_of_Systems.content: Reports fever earlier in illness, now improving.
Reports shortness of breath on exertion and none at rest.
Review_of_Systems.source_text: SOB on exertion; none at rest
